newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks Vancouver labor deal ratified. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Starbucks Vancouver labor deal ratified. [CORRECTED 23:15 GMT]

text.p: Starbucks Corp. said on Tuesday that 110 unionized workers in Vancouver ratified the coffee retailer's first ever union accord, which includes a provision basing pay increases on merit rather than seniority.

Seattle-based Starbucks said in a statement that under the two-year contract deal struck last week, employees "do not get automatic incremental pay increases based on predetermined dates in a contract.
"Instead, performance, skills and abilities will be considered for an employee-partner at Starbucks to progress from the minimum hourly pay to the maximum."
The two-year contract raises unionized workers' pay to a C$7.75 (US$5.56) hourly base rate from C$7 (US$5.11), with a C12 cent (US8.8 cent) an hour increase on July 1, 1998.

The Canadian Auto Workers union, which represents the unionized workers in eight coffee bars and a bakery distribution center in Vancouver, had demanded a C$10 (US$7.30) an hour starting wage. (Corrects from increase of C$10.)
Starbucks said that non-union employees in its other British Columbia stores would get the same basic pay increase as the unionized stores.
The 1,100-outlet Starbucks chain has more than 1,400 non-union employees in 87 other stores in British Columbia.
